source.title: Deep learning via message passing algorithms based on belief propagation
source.authors: Carlo Lucibello; Fabrizio Pittorino; Gabriele Perugini; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests message-passing training on natural image datasets and reports training and test error, optimizer comparisons, network sizes, sparsity, and a perturbation-based local-energy measure. It extends the generalization-gap discussion to binary-weight and binary-activation MLPs trained with message passing.
record.gate_note: The study reports natural-label training and test results, but does not train on random labels or test whether memorization capacity coexists with generalization. It reports test error and train error in separate tables and plots, but does not directly test the width beyond interpolation claim, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, adaptive optimizer generalization claims, or dropout. Local energy measures change in training error under random weight flips; it is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7. No example-removal experiment tests V8.
record.test_reason: Appendix B.6 explicitly reports that Adam gives slightly better training and test performance than plain SGD in the Figure 2 experiments. This bears on V4 in binary-activation MLPs, although the optimizer tuning protocol and numerical Adam–SGD difference are not supplied. The main message-passing comparisons do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: PasP message passing trains deep and wide binary-activation MLPs with performance broadly comparable to SGD-based baselines, with advantages in some sparse and continual-learning settings. Approximate Bayesian predictions improve over point estimates. Weight-flip measurements indicate relatively flat solutions, but do not directly compute local entropy or establish V7; theoretical understanding and exact posterior inference remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses posterior-as-prior message passing and BP-derived updates rather than standard gradient training; BinaryNet is included as an SGD-based comparator. Networks use binary activations and binary or continuous weights, without biases or batch normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by message-passing algorithm and dataset; sparsity changes final test accuracy. The authors report sensitivity of BP dynamics mainly to ρ and α and say tuning ρ by layer can improve generalization in some cases. Batch size from 1 to 1024 is said to give consistent results, but detailed accuracy values for that range are not tabulated.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 compares natural-label training errors of BP, AMP, MF, and BinaryNet; Table 1 reports mostly comparable test errors despite often lower message-passing training errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Message-passing algorithms can train binary MLPs with held-out performance broadly comparable to a modified BinaryNet baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B.5 measures training-error increases under random binary weight flips and describes relatively flat solutions for both BP and BinaryNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BP and BinaryNet solutions tolerate random binary weight flips; this does not establish V7's relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper reports advantages from locally Bayesian predictions, sparse-network training, and continual-learning retention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Message-passing performance depends on prediction procedure and learning setting.

record.code_released: not stated; implementation is described as provided in an anonymous GitHub repo
record.problems: The study does not use random labels, so it cannot test memorization capacity against natural-label generalization. Core results are comparisons of message-passing algorithms with a modified BinaryNet baseline, and the reported architecture and dataset sweeps do not isolate the claim-version interventions. Some stated batch-size consistency is not accompanied by tabulated performance values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the selected direct training results. Local-energy profiles in Appendix B.5/Figure 7 are not entered because the relevant V7 measure requires magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and ranking of generalization gaps; the reported plot instead measures training-error change under binary flips. Other figure-only training curves are not transcribed into rows because exact per-epoch values are not reported in text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and random-label held-out accuracy; natural-label results alone cannot establish coexistence.
Test-error behavior as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold; the architecture experiments do not isolate this comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Whether the Adam–SGD comparison uses only learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning, weight-decay changes, optimizer switching, and language benchmarks.

Held-out performance across batch sizes under a documented fixed epoch budget and the effects of recipe adaptations. Cross-method comparability at each batch size does not establish a within-method batch-size penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Identifying memorized examples and comparing their removal with random removal followed by retraining.

missing.what: Adam versus plain SGD comparison: the authors explicitly report slightly better training and test performance with Adam. Add the qualitative comparison, distinguish binary and continuous weights if supported, and mark the numerical difference and optimizer tuning protocol as unspecified.
missing.locator: Appendix B.6, final sentence; Section 4.4 and Figure 2

record.verdict_notes: The extraction overlooks the explicit Adam–SGD statement in Appendix B.6. All 24 numerical values match Table 2, but none measures a listed version's effect; their observed states should not be interpreted as claim evidence. Table 1 and Table 2 captions incorrectly name only Fashion-MNIST, whereas their body rows cover six dataset/task settings.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy is tested.
No width sweep around or beyond the zero-training-error threshold tests test-error behavior.
The study uses fully connected MLPs; it does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out performance under the version's tuning conditions.
Batch sizes are discussed for training performance, but there is no fixed-epoch batch-size generalization-gap comparison of the kind in this version.

The local-energy measurement flips a random fraction of binary weights and measures training-error change; it does not use magnitude-scaled perturbations or rank generalization gaps among networks matched for training loss.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison is performed.
